feed.title: NPR Topics: Politics
feed.subtitle: Follow NPR Politics for nonpartisan coverage of government, elections, policy debates and voting rights. Plus weekday audio from The NPR Politics Podcast.

entry.title: Trump administration attempting to prosecute former FBI Director James Comey again
entry.summary: The Trump administration is attempting to prosecute James Comey for what it calls a decade-old leak of classified information. Comey's lawyers immediately dismissed the effort as invalid and outside the time limit.

entry.title: Judge says DOJ illegally fired the daughter of former FBI director Comey
entry.summary: Maurene Comey served as a federal prosecutor in Manhattan for around a decade. A judicial ruling finding her dismissal unlawful adds to concerns of politically motivated firings at the DOJ.

entry.title: Redistricting isn't playing out how the GOP hoped. And, Brazil's Lula wins 4th term
entry.summary: Republicans are spending millions on the midterms, and they still may not win districts drawn to favor them. And, Brazil's Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva won a fourth term in a stunning political comeback.

entry.title: Political consultant on the impact of Republicans' gerrymandering efforts
entry.summary: NPR's Leila Fadel speaks with political consultant Mike Madrid about how Republicans' gerrymandering efforts have backfired.

entry.title: Trump escalates anti-Muslim attacks against El-Sayed in Michigan
entry.summary: President Trump intensified his anti-Muslim rhetoric against Michigan Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed on Sunday, portraying him as a threat to national security and questioning his loyalty to the United States.

entry.title: Republicans are spending millions and still may not win districts drawn to favor them
entry.summary: Republicans redrew congressional district lines to try to tilt the midterms in their favor. But now they are facing expensive and competitive races they had hoped to outmaneuver.

entry.title: Blanche defends DOJ lawsuit blocking Alaska Senate results if Republican loses
entry.summary: Attorney General Todd Blanche defended the Justice Department's suit over Alaska's Senate race in an interview on CNN.

entry.title: Politics chat: The polls show a Democratic sweep in the midterms. Can you trust them?
entry.summary: If you look at the few truly competitive seats, polls show a more complicated picture of momentum toward the Democratic Party in midterm House races. For the Senate, Republicans are on defense.

entry.title: Democrats see an opportunity to tilt Pennsylvania's state legislature their way
entry.summary: Statehouse elections this fall could swing the balance of power in state capitals. In Pennsylvania, Democrats could take control of what has been a divided legislature.

entry.title: Independent candidates sense a moment. Some Democrats hope they're right
entry.summary: As they look to win the Senate, Democrats are hoping that independent candidates in Nebraska and Montana can help them topple Republicans in a part of the country where their own brand is hurting.
